segments.t: Now Gabriel comes out to reception with Hervé: a casting director, Caroline Braudel, has chosen two photos from the agency's envelope, and one of them is Sofia, the receptionist. We'll hear it in French first; don't worry about catching every word.
Sofia, tu as mis ta photo dans cette enveloppe?
Oui! Et elle me veut pour le casting!
Non, Sofia! Tu n'es pas dans notre agence.
Et je ne sais pas si tu sais jouer.
Tu ne sais pas? Alors viens voir mon spectacle!
Personne ne me propose d'auditions!
Mais là, tu as volé cette audition!
Non, j'ai juste ajouté ma photo, c'est tout.
Elle veut me voir? Elle aime mon look?
Calme-toi, Sofia! Allô, Laura?
Gabriel, on parle! J'ai invité tout le monde à mon spectacle.
Et personne n'est venu!
Une seconde, Laura, s'il te plaît.
Ça suffit! Je viendrai voir ton spectacle, d'accord?
Tu viens me voir? Merci!
Promesse d'agent! Oui, Laura, je suis à toi.
Let's go back through the argument. Gabriel holds up the envelope of actors' photos in front of Sofia.
Sofia, tu as mis ta photo dans cette enveloppe?
'Sofia, did you put your photo in this envelope?' The everyday past tense of 'to put' uses a short past form after 'have'.
Oui! Et elle me veut pour le casting!
'Yes! And she wants me for the casting!' Sofia isn't sorry at all: the casting director actually picked her.
Non, Sofia! Tu n'es pas dans notre agence.
'No, Sofia! You're not with our agency.' Literally 'in our agency'. Sofia works on the front desk, not as one of their clients.
Et je ne sais pas si tu sais jouer.
'And I don't know if you can act.' Notice the same verb, 'to know', used twice: first 'know a fact', then 'know how to act'.
Tu ne sais pas? Alors viens voir mon spectacle!
'You don't know? Then come and see my show!' The command 'come' is followed straight by 'to see', with no little word in between.
Personne ne me propose d'auditions!
'Nobody offers me auditions!' With the word for 'nobody' at the start, French doesn't use the usual second negative word.
Mais là, tu as volé cette audition!
'But here, you stole this audition!' The verb 'to steal' in the everyday past tense. Sofia objects to the word.
Non, j'ai juste ajouté ma photo, c'est tout.
'No, I just added my photo, that's all.' The two words at the end literally say 'it is all', a very common way to finish an excuse.
Elle veut me voir? Elle aime mon look?
'Does she want to see me? Does she like my look?' Even while arguing, Sofia is thrilled that a casting director noticed her.
Calme-toi, Sofia!
'Calm down, Sofia!' Literally 'calm yourself'. Then Gabriel's phone rings: it's Laura Smet.
Allô, Laura?
'Hello, Laura?' That opening greeting is used only on the telephone. Sofia doesn't care that he's on a call.
Gabriel, on parle! J'ai invité tout le monde à mon spectacle.
'Gabriel, we're talking! I invited everyone to my show.' In the episode she says she invited Mathias, Andréa, and even the old lady with her dog.
Et personne n'est venu!
'And nobody came!' The verb 'to come' makes its past tense with 'is' rather than 'has'.
Une seconde, Laura, s'il te plaît.
'One second, Laura, please.' He uses the casual 'please' with his client Laura, then turns back to Sofia to get some peace.
Ça suffit! Je viendrai voir ton spectacle, d'accord?
'That's enough! I'll come and see your show, okay?' The first two words mean 'it suffices', and then he uses the future tense of 'to come'.
Tu viens me voir? Merci!
'You'll come and see me? Thank you!' Sofia lights up at once, using the present tense for the near future.
Promesse d'agent! Oui, Laura, je suis à toi.
'An agent's promise! Yes, Laura, I'm with you.' Literally 'promise of agent', without an article, and then 'I am to you' as he goes back to his phone call. Let's listen to the whole scene once more.
Sofia, tu as mis ta photo dans cette enveloppe?
Oui! Et elle me veut pour le casting!
Non, Sofia! Tu n'es pas dans notre agence.
Et je ne sais pas si tu sais jouer.
Tu ne sais pas? Alors viens voir mon spectacle!
Personne ne me propose d'auditions!
Mais là, tu as volé cette audition!
Non, j'ai juste ajouté ma photo, c'est tout.
Elle veut me voir? Elle aime mon look?
Calme-toi, Sofia! Allô, Laura?
Gabriel, on parle! J'ai invité tout le monde à mon spectacle.
Et personne n'est venu!
Une seconde, Laura, s'il te plaît.
Ça suffit! Je viendrai voir ton spectacle, d'accord?
Tu viens me voir? Merci!
Promesse d'agent! Oui, Laura, je suis à toi.
Sofia has wrung a promise out of Gabriel at last, and now he has Laura Smet on the line. Listen out for how the word for 'nobody' works without the second negative word. See you next time!
Bonne soirée!
